title: M3.3 Portable Review Handoff design
purpose: Redefine M3.3 from redundant LLM assistance into a provider-neutral deterministic portable handoff and re-entry layer between author and independent reviewer contexts.
invariants: M3.3 adds no new semantic authority; M3.2/M3.2.5 authorities remain upstream and read-only.
M3.3 contains no model/provider API, credential, chat runtime or learner-runtime AI.
Review handoffs are transient external evidence artifacts and are not a Git corpus.
Author scratchpad, hidden reasoning and active author context are excluded by interface design.
Exact admitted source bytes and exact FactoryContext hashes bind every handoff.
A candidate change invalidates the prior review and requires a fresh independent review.
M3.3 does not implement human graphical review debt #272.
M3.4, Gate3, Gate4 and M4+ remain HOLD.
requiredEvidence: Design explicitly rejects redundant LLM/provider integration.
Design freezes prepare-review and consume-review responsibilities without duplicating semantic rules.
Design requires deterministic portable ZIP identity, path independence and exact skill/source/context binding.
Design freezes disjoint implementation and independent-QA scopes.
No product/runtime/workflow/contract change in the design PR.
adversarialTests: Attempt to package source bytes whose SourceAdmission is HOLD.
Move identical inputs to different host paths.
Tamper candidate, brief, source, skill, request or manifest bytes.
Inject undeclared or traversal ZIP members.
Import a stale review after candidate repair.
Use review evidence source IDs outside the handoff allowlist.
Set authorScratchpadSeen or authorActiveContextReused to true.
Try to convert a semantic HOLD to PASS in the handoff layer.
Attempt to package author scratchpad/chat/log files.
Attempt to add model/provider or learner-runtime behavior.
independentReview: Repository governance and PR scope verify the design-only boundary.
Future QA-WP-023 must be disjoint and non-repairing.
rollback: Revert the two design files only. Promoted M3.2/M3.2.5 behavior remains unchanged.
